claim: Pretraining one locomotion policy on pooled data from many different robot bodies with offline reinforcement learning, rather than behaviour cloning, pays off when much of the pooled data is suboptimal, and the pooled pretraining speeds up learning on a robot left out of it. Supported only if, averaged over the pooled datasets that are mostly suboptimal, the offline-RL policy earns higher return than behaviour cloning with the same network, while the two are within noise on expert-only data; and if, for every held-out robot tested, starting from the pooled pretrained network reaches a good policy in fewer updates than training that robot from scratch.

experiments: Build a pooled multi-robot locomotion benchmark with controlled data quality. Setup: 16 simulated robots in MuJoCo (nine quadrupeds, six bipeds, one hexapod), each trained with PPO to walk at a commanded 1 m/s forward or backward under a shared dense reward with robot-specific weights. For each robot and direction build three 1M-step datasets: expert rollouts of the converged policy, the whole training replay up to expert level (about 500M steps) subsampled uniformly, and a mix of 700k early, suboptimal steps with 300k late steps. A single network takes a shared observation part plus variable-length joint and foot sets aggregated by attention conditioned on morphology descriptors, extended with an action encoder for a Q-function. Each method uses about 100M sampled transitions per robot; report final return, mean +/- standard error over 5 seeds.

Compare offline RL with behaviour cloning on pooled data. Setup: implicit Q-learning and behaviour cloning with the same architecture, trained on all 16 robots for each of the six datasets. Result: on expert data they tie (63.39 vs 63.31 forward, 67.10 vs 67.17 backward); on replay data offline RL wins (54.61 vs 49.71, 51.86 vs 42.87); on the mostly-suboptimal data it wins forward (36.62 vs 30.52) but loses backward (38.69 vs 41.42). Means are 52.05 against 49.17.

Test whether pooled pretraining helps a robot it did not include. Setup: leave-one-out: pretrain with offline RL on the pooled data minus one robot, then fine-tune on that robot, against training on that robot from scratch; plot evaluation return against update steps for a quadruped (Badger) and two bipeds (Unitree G1, Cassie). Result: the pretrained network converges markedly faster for all three.
